options.content: Show data from each individual run from the last seven days.
Transfer size is the size over the wire when the data is transferred to the browser (hopefully compressed). Content size is the size unpacked in the browser.
Showing how the page is built over time.
Variation over time in the CPU benchmark metric (the time it takes to run a JavaScript loop). Use this metric to make sure the CPU speed is constant over time.
Variation over time in the time to first byte metric (TTFB). Use it to make sure TTFB is stable over time.
Screenshots showing what part of the page is the largest contentful paint (LCP) (the red area) and content that is moved around (cumulative layout shift).
Largest contentful paint (LCP) - the largest area painted is in the red area.
Cumulative layout shift (CLS) - red is the area that moved.
Main document timings is the timings for downloading the main HTML page.

Data that is collected using the [Navigation Timing API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Navigation_timing_API) (the same data as you can collect from real users). Use it to compare changes in data from our real users.

Data collected using the [CPU long tasks API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Long_Tasks_API). The long tasks depends on the CPU used on the device that runs the tests so you can only compare metrics using the exact same device. Use the data to see trends.

Performance metrics that you can add yourself by annotating your page. We automatically collect [User Timing API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/User_Timing_API) metrics and [Element Timing API metrics](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Element_timing_API) (when elements are painted on the screen).
Keep track of the number of elements that need style recalculation before first contentful paint and largest contentful paint.
The coach helps you find performance problems on your web page.
Delta TTFB metrics is metrics where we remove the time to first byte from the metrics. If we have metrics that are unstable because of unstable TTFB these metrics can be stable.
Data collected from the Chrome trace log, where we can see where the browser spends its time creating the page.

spec.title: First Contentful Paint
spec.description: Each test is the $function of the runs and the band shows the fastest and slowest run. The background shows what Google calls good (green), needs improvement (yellow) and poor (red). The thick line is the average of the last 24 hours, the dashed line is the same average one week earlier and the dotted line is the trend over the time range.
